task: Make the demo behave like a real meeting and fix what Steve watched go wrong: text arriving in blocks instead of word by word, two summary cards landing at once, one sentence split across two cards, and lines well past the 14-word display limit

public/services/transcription/demo.js.summary: Streams word by word at MS_PER_WORD (145 wpm) with a deterministic length-derived inter-sentence pause, replacing per-utterance partial bursts separated by multi-second delayMs gaps. DEMO_SCRIPT entries are now {text} only; pacing is derived. Script wording also changed at Steve's instruction for an LDS audience: nothing is served or eaten anywhere in it (no morning tea, no shared-plate lunch, no meal on a doorstep -- the quiet act of service is now a lift to an appointment and a mown lawn).

public/services/summary-prompt.js.summary: Exports SUMMARY_MAX_WORDS = 14 and interpolates it into the prompt, which previously carried the limit only as the English sentence 'Maximum 14 words.' -- so the demo summarizer could and did use its own budget, putting lines on the wall about twice that long with nothing to catch it.

public/services/summarization/demo.js.summary: Returns exactly ONE earliest unshown complete sentence per tick (a joined line was re-split by the display's own wrap, so two cards appeared in the same instant and the first summary looked skipped). Honours SUMMARY_MAX_WORDS via fitToWordLimit, which shortens at a clause boundary and falls back to a word boundary only when the first clause is already too long -- never mid-word, never an added ellipsis, always a byte-for-byte prefix of what was said. Filler stripping narrowed to hesitation sounds only: it was removing 'so'/'and'/'but' and beheading real sentences. Uses the shared TERMINAL_END so quote-terminated sentences are eligible.

public/services/transcript-bucket.js.summary: TERMINAL_END is now exported (it had been duplicated in three slightly different spellings, two accepting a closing quote and one not). New takeSendableChunks(consumable, maxChars) returns the oldest run of chunks that fits the send cap, so what is sent and what is consumed are the same set -- bucketText slices to the LAST maxChars, so consuming a whole large backlog destroyed its head without ever summarizing it.

public/controller/runtime.js.summary: summarizeCurrentText sends only takeSendableChunks(consumable) and no longer includes the bucket remainder or the live partial preview. Sending an unfinished trailing sentence let a fragment become a display line, and its tail came round again next tick and was summarized a second time on its own -- both halves of the sentence-split-across-two-cards report.

public/services/transcript-display.js.summary: AI-sourced lines are segmented at AI_LINE_SAFETY_MAX_CHARS (240) rather than the 120-char default, so an obedient 14-word line (~90 chars) is never re-wrapped while a summarizer that ignores its limit is still bounded rather than producing one enormous card. splitBySentence no longer treats a title or initial as a sentence end -- 'Bro. Smith will speak' was rendering a card containing only 'Bro.', and Bro./Sis./Pres. are everyday words in this room.

public/controller/transcript-resize.js.summary: Persists a user-dragged #railTranscript height (localStorage 'railTranscriptHeight', clamped) via ResizeObserver, restoring it on boot. Skips the observe()-time first callback, which would otherwise overwrite a taller saved preference with whatever the current window can render. Inert at <=900px so a desktop height cannot corrupt the bottom sheet's measured snap points.

public/controller/start-app.js.summary: Wires applyPersistedTranscriptHeight before bindEvents, and bindTranscriptResize within it.

public/styles/layout.css.summary: .railTranscript gains resize: vertical and a max-height of min(28rem, 60vh) so dragging can actually accomplish something. The box must stay padding- and border-free: the persisted height round-trips content-box against border-box.

public/styles/responsive.css.summary: Inside <=900px: resize: none plus height: auto !important, neutralising any persisted inline height inside the quick-controls sheet.

test/server/provider-keys.test.js.summary: Constructs the app explicitly key-less. createApp defaults openaiClient/anthropicApiKey from process.env, so the test asserted different things depending on whether the developer had a real key in .env -- it broke the morning Steve added one.

flow_impact: Changes the summarize flow's payload contract (sent set == consumed set, complete sentences only) and the display flow's segmentation for AI lines. Verified live with Demo + Demo at a 5s interval and no paid calls: cards arrive one at a time, in spoken order, 5/9/7 words, punctuation preserved, no ellipsis.
